content: Pants Pankuro is a series of animated shorts originating from Japan, specifically designed for toddlers and young children. Each episode is slightly over a minute long and is broadcast on Japanese public television. The primary focus of the series is to address the challenges and learning processes associated with toilet training. The show features anthropomorphic characters, such as talking toilets and washing machines, who provide guidance to children on proper restroom habits and how to handle accidents. The main character, Pants Pankuro, is a young boy approximately three years old. He has recently transitioned to wearing underpants and is in the early stages of learning how to use the toilet. Pankuro has a younger sister named Komingo, who has not yet begun toilet training. Another character, Koricchi, is a boy of the same age as Pankuro. Koricchi and Pankuro share a competitive relationship. Koin, a girl also around Pankuro's age, enjoys spinning and dancing. Toire-sama, a friendly household toilet, plays a significant role in the series. Pankuro treats Toire-sama with a high level of respect, akin to how one might regard an elder family member. Kamiko-san, the toilet roll holder, is another character in the series. Sentako Hacchan, an eight-legged washing machine, is enthusiastic about doing laundry. The name Sentako Hacchan is derived from the Japanese words sentaku (laundry) and tako (octopus). Additionally, Koricchi's family owns an old-fashioned squat toilet, though its name is not specified in the series.
